title: DataTransfer.setDragImage() steps are unclear on how to size passed in

labels.name: topic: drag and drop
labels.description: Drag and drop, DataTransfer and the drag events

body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? Step 3 in [DataTransfer.setDragImage()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dnd.html#dom-datatransfer-setdragimage) states: > 3. If image is an [img](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#the-img-element) element, then set the [drag data store bitmap](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dnd.html#drag-data-store-bitmap) to the element's image (at its [natural size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions)); otherwise, set the [drag data store bitmap](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dnd.html#drag-data-store-bitmap) to an image generated from the given element (the exact mechanism for doing so is not currently specified). For images that don't have a natural size, like dimensionless SVG images or an `` with `content: linear-gradient(...)`, its unclear what to do here. For the most part, places where images need to be sized and displayed in some way like this should specify a [concrete object size resolution](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-size-resolution) algorithm to use. Here though, I think it might make more sense to just defer to the engine so they can use whatever rules they use of drag-and-drop of images elsewhere. Or, if there is spec text about the normal (non-script) drag-and-drop of images, defer to that. The one case that might be worth calling out is what to do about an `` that is detached from the DOM, as that won't be handled in the non-script case. For that case, my suggestion would be to use the [default sizing algorithm](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-sizing) but allowing engines to set reasonable limits on maximum and minimum concrete sizes.
